sources.title: The activity lifecycle
locators: Saving and restoring transient UI state, 271–302
sources.supported_facts: Keep onPause brief; the current guide advises against using it for saves, network requests or database transactions. Persist during suitable foreground opportunities, with onStop as fallback. Configuration-driven Activity destruction is not equivalent to the end of an application process.
sources.limits: Current Compose-first guide; use lifecycle principles only, not a requirement to rewrite a native game with Compose. No deadline, completion or universal durability guarantee.

sources.title: Processes and app lifecycle
sources.supported_facts: The system controls process lifetime. Cached processes may be killed without onDestroy. From Android 13, a process may receive limited or no execution time until active again. An ordinary in-process worker is not independent of process death.
sources.limits: Do not prescribe a foreground service or job API as an automatic save fix. The page supplies process-lifecycle constraints, not a game checkpoint transaction protocol.

sources.title: Activity API reference
sources.supported_facts: If onSaveInstanceState is called, targets starting at P/API 28 receive it after onStop; earlier targets receive it before onStop, without a guaranteed order relative to onPause. It is omitted in some lifecycle transitions. Since Honeycomb targets, ordinary killability begins after onStop returns; extreme memory pressure remains an exception.
sources.limits: Target SDK conditions are not merely device OS conditions. Older general onPause-saving prose is retained on this reference; use S1 for current workload guidance, rather than combining the paragraphs into a synchronous save recipe.

sources.title: Save UI states
locators: Hook into saved state using SavedStateRegistry, 176–180 and 245
Use local persistence to handle process death for complex or large data, 246–249
Managing UI state / Restore complex states, 250–269
sources.supported_facts: ViewModel survives configuration changes but not system process death. Saved state supports small transient recovery data, not long-term app storage; persistent storage covers retained app data. Complete dismissal and finish differ from system recreation. SavedStateRegistry writes while stopped are not saved without another onStart/onStop cycle.
sources.limits: No fixed universal Bundle payload-size budget is established here. Saved state is not a durable game-save receipt. Do not apply SavedStateRegistry timing to an unrelated engine callback without integration evidence.

sources.title: GameActivity
locators: Release locations / Contents of Jetpack library, 224–241
sources.supported_facts: Java-side GameActivity interaction and JNI enqueue app-cycle events to native_app_glue; game code consumes the queue on the glue native thread. The Java and native layers must be distinguished.
sources.limits: The overview calls GameActivity a descendant of NativeActivity but also says it derives from AppCompatActivity; avoid relying on the ambiguous first phrase as a Java inheritance claim. No AAR version or packaged source was inspected.

scope: Current first-party documentation and original checkpoint42/pending43 reasoning. No device, emulator, engine, package implementation, persistent-write or power-loss tests.
scope_limits: Missing completion acknowledgment does not prove a failed commit
Target SDK conditions differ from device OS identity
UI recovery is not durable game-save completion
Native integration is an ownership caution, not a cross-engine recipe
